faqs.question: What is a safety barrel for in-plant use?
faqs.answer: It's a stainless steel container built primarily for storing bigger volumes of flammable liquid, with filling and metering available as a secondary capability, and removable flame traps and a pressure control valve for protection.

faqs.question: Can this barrel be used for off-site transport?
faqs.answer: No. This product is certified for in-plant use only; off-site transport requires a separately certified transportation barrel.

faqs.question: Which sizes are stackable?
faqs.answer: The 25 and 50-liter barrels specifically. This isn't stated for the 10-liter size or for the 100 and 200-liter sizes.

faqs.question: What is a safety collection barrel?
faqs.answer: A different barrel purpose entirely, built to receive liquid, such as waste or a contained spill, using a centered 2-inch plug rather than a dispensing mechanism.

faqs.question: How do I decide between a dispensing barrel and a collection barrel?
faqs.answer: Choose a dispensing barrel, with a screw cap, tap, or metering device, if you're storing and controlling liquid coming out; choose a collection barrel if you're receiving liquid, such as for waste or spill containment.

faqs.question: How do I find the exact order number for my requirement?
faqs.answer: Confirm your purpose (dispensing or collection), your size, and whether you need a content indicator; for example, a 25-liter barrel with a self-closing tap and content indicator is order number 25ZI.

faqs.question: Are 100 and 200-liter barrels available?
faqs.answer: Yes, across all barrel types, though specific order numbers for these sizes are confirmed directly by Inkarp rather than listed in the standard order table.

faqs.question: What is a content indicator?
faqs.answer: A feature that shows the fill level without needing to open the barrel, available on tap, metering device, and collection variants.

faqs.question: Can the flame traps be serviced?
faqs.answer: Yes. They're removable, supporting inspection and maintenance rather than replacing the entire barrel.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Safety Barrels for In-Plant Use in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on the size, configuration, and whether you need dispensing or collection. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

longForm.heroLead: Some flammable liquids need to be dispensed carefully. Others just need to be stored in bulk, safely, without eating up warehouse floor space. This barrel is built for the second job first. Stainless steel from 0.8 to 1.5 mm, scaled to the size, with removable flame traps and a pressure control valve venting from around 0.3 bar. The 25 and 50-liter sizes stack, so bulk storage doesn't mean spreading out. It still dispenses when you need it to, with a screw cap, a self-closing tap, or a metering device with separate ventilation. Content indicators let you check the fill level without opening the barrel at all. There's also a genuinely different variant: the safety collection barrel, built to receive liquid rather than dispense it, for waste or spill containment. This barrel is for in-plant use. Off-site transport needs a certified transportation barrel instead.

sections.title: Safety Barrels for In-Plant Use at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate these barrels: what stacking actually saves, how a dispensing barrel differs from a collection barrel, what sizes and order numbers are available, and Inkarp installation and service support.
sections.subheading: Storage comes first here, dispensing second.
body: This line is built primarily for storing bigger volumes of flammable liquid, with filling and metering as a secondary, still-fully-usable capability.
Stacking is real, and it's specific. The 25 and 50-liter barrels are stackable; that claim isn't made for the 10-liter size or for the 100 and 200-liter sizes.
The size range goes further than the order number table shows. All barrel types are also available in 100 and 200 liters, though specific order numbers for those sizes aren't listed here.
Two barrels do two different jobs. A dispensing barrel controls how liquid comes out; a collection barrel is built to receive liquid, for waste or spill containment, a genuinely different purpose.
You can check the level without opening it. Content indicators are available on the tap, metering device, and collection barrel variants.
Construction scales with size. Stainless steel thickness runs 0.8 to 1.5 mm, with removable flame traps for inspection and service.
This is an in-plant product, and that boundary holds here too. Off-site transport requires a certified transportation barrel, a separate Rötzmeier line.

Configuration note: Confirmed line is the Rötzmeier Safety Barrels - for in-plant use. Confirmed sizes with order numbers are 10, 25 and 50 liters. Also available: 100 and 200 liters, with specific order numbers confirmed by Inkarp. Stackable: 25 and 50-liter sizes specifically. Not certified for off-site transport - a separate product line covers that requirement. Full specifications (exact dimensions, weight, additional certification detail) are available on request from Inkarp.

sections.title: Technical Specifications
body: The technical specifications of the Safety Barrels for In-Plant Use include 0.8 to 1.5 mm stainless steel construction, size-specific stackability, and seven distinct configurations.
Storing a bigger volume safely is a different problem from dispensing a smaller one carefully, and this line is built around that first.

Stacking is the clearest example. At 25 and 50 liters, barrels stack, which turns a warehouse floor space problem into a vertical one instead. That claim doesn't extend to the 10-liter size, which doesn't need it as much, or to the 100 and 200-liter sizes, which are confirmed available but not confirmed stackable. Content indicators solve a related problem: knowing how much is left without opening a barrel that's specifically built to stay sealed.
Product expert note: Tell our team your storage volume and warehouse layout, and Inkarp will confirm whether stacking applies to your size and what floor space it actually saves.

sections.title: Dispensing, Collection and Order Numbers
body: The first decision isn't size. It's whether you're dispensing liquid out of the barrel, or collecting liquid into it.

For bulk storage with occasional simple access, specify the screw cap variant. For controlled, repeated dispensing, specify a self-closing tap or metering device. To check fill level without opening, add a content indicator variant. For collecting waste or spill liquid rather than dispensing, specify the collection barrel, with or without a level indicator. For larger-volume dispensing beyond 10 liters, use the screw cap or tap variants at 25 or 50 liters.
Product expert note: Send our team whether you're dispensing or collecting, your required volume, and whether you need a content indicator, and Inkarp will confirm the exact order number.
